title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In these continuation pages of the 'Longue Marche' Grothendieck builds, over a base S0 (essentially Spec Z, with special attention to characteristics 2 and 3), a group scheme Z~_{ρ,σ}. The neighbouring pages fix its ingredients.

- M is a free Z-module of rank 2 with basis λ0, λ1.
- ρ_M has order 3: λ0 ↦ λ1 ↦ -λ0-λ1. This is checked by formula (60) of the next page, which gives (1-ρ)(a0λ0+a1λ1) = (a0+a1)λ0 + (2a1-a0)λ1.
- σ_M swaps λ0 and λ1, i.e. σ(λ0)=λ1.
- Primed versions ρ', σ' act on a Heisenberg-type extension 𝔖^+ of M.

This is the genus-1 / modular setting: the elliptic automorphisms of order 3 (or 6) and 2 (or 4) attached to the special j-values j=0 and j=1728. These points collide precisely in characteristics 2 and 3.

The previous page finishes constructing Z~_{ρ,σ} as a scheme (a 'groupoid') with morphisms:
- ν' : Z~ → G_0,
- ν2 : Z~ → {0,1}_{S0},
- μ = 4ν' + 2 + ν2 (as written there),
- signs ε2, ε3 : Z~ → μ_2 = {±1}.

This page does the following.

(52) A morphism of sheaves on S0, Z~_{ρ,σ} → Aut_gr(𝔖^+), sending a structure u (underlined) to the underlying automorphism u.

(53) Combined with the 'multiplier' and the two signs, this gives Z~_{ρ,σ} → Aut_gr(𝔖^+) × G_m × μ × μ, u ↦ (u, μ(u), ε2(u), ε3(u)). The map is asserted to be a monomorphism. Grothendieck says that calculations 'already done thirty-six times in various contexts' should show it is a homomorphism for a unique group structure on Z~. His uniqueness argument: the structure is known in characteristic ≠ 2,3 (where Z~ is presumably nicer), and one extends by schematic density.

This yields an extension 1 → Z~^{+0} → Z~ → G_m × μ × μ → 1. A marginal note calls this 'un peu canular' and suggests the projection could be read off directly from M×M via (α0,β0) ↦ (1-ρ)α0, (1-σ)β0, 'but not pretty'.

(55) Explicitly, the neutral part is the closed subgroup scheme
Z~^{+0} = {(α0,β0,γ') ∈ M×M×G_a | 4γ' = 0, (1-ρ_M)α0 = (1-σ_M)β0 + 2γ'λ1}.
Here M×M means the vector group V of M⊗O.

(56) Projecting to γ' gives 1 → Z~^{+00} → Z~^{+0} → _4G_a → 1.
- _4G_a = ker(4 : G_a → G_a) is a non-flat group scheme over Z.
- It is trivial over Z[1/2] and equals G_a in characteristic 2.

Next page. The kernel Z~^{+00} (written +∞ there) is {(α0,β0) | (1-ρ)α0 = (1-σ)β0}. Grothendieck shows it is V(P), with P the rank-2 kernel of (1-ρ, -(1-σ)) : M² → M. He first says this map is surjective, then corrects himself: its image is {c0λ0+c1λ1 | c0+c1 ≡ 0 mod 3}, of index 3. Hence the kernel group scheme is smooth of relative dimension 2 only away from characteristic 3.

Purpose. The page computes, integrally over Z, the structure of a centralizer-type group scheme of automorphisms of a genus-one 'Heisenberg' fundamental-group-like object compatible with the elliptic symmetries ρ, σ. The pathologies at 2 and 3 are made explicit through _4G_a and the index-3 cokernel. This presumably serves the description of the elliptic part of the Teichmüller tower / the action of Gal or GT-type groups on genus-1 data.
errors: (55) is transcribed with (1+ρ_M)α0. The next page, (57)/(59), uses (1-ρ_M)α0, which is consistent with the rest of the computation, so the sign is (1-ρ) (or the transcription misreads it).
The first equation of (55) reads 'α0 4γ'=0'. In context it can only be 4γ'=0, since the quotient in (56) is _4G_a.

On the next page Grothendieck first claims M×M → M is surjective, then corrects it. The image has index 3 (c0+c1 = 3a1), so the sequence (59) is not right-exact as written. This is why smoothness fails in characteristic 3, as he notes in the margin.

The group structure on Z~ is not proved on this page. It is deferred to 'calculs déjà faits trente six fois', plus a uniqueness-by-schematic-density argument. Density holds only if Z~ is flat (or its characteristic ≠2,3 locus is schematically dense), and Z~ contains non-flat pieces such as _4G_a. So the density argument as stated is a gap: it gives uniqueness only on the closure of the generic part, not on all of Z~.

ideas.what: Group scheme over Z of automorphisms of a rank-2 Heisenberg-type group compatible with order-3 and order-2/4 automorphisms ρ, σ, with multiplier μ ∈ G_m and two sign characters ε2, ε3.
ideas.modern_name: Integral centralizer / similitude group scheme of a Heisenberg group with elliptic (j=0, j=1728) symmetries
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not specifically attributed; related to theta groups (Mumford) and integral models of automorphism groups.
ideas.where_published: The published part of La Longue Marche (Malgoire edition) treats genus-1 Galois actions, but these specific pages (650bis–787) appear unpublished.

ideas.what: Fixing the group law on a scheme by an embedding into a group scheme, with uniqueness via schematic density from the characteristic ≠ 2,3 locus.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of group structures by schematic density (EGA IV §11.10, SGA 3)

ideas.what: Dévissage of the identity part as an extension of the non-flat group scheme _4G_a by a vector-group kernel V(P), smooth outside characteristic 3 because coker(1-ρ, σ-1) ≅ Z/3.
ideas.modern_name: Non-flat kernel group schemes; vector group V(P) of a module; bad reduction at 2 and 3 for the elliptic automorphisms

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an integral (over Z, characteristics 2 and 3 included) group-scheme description of the symmetry group of genus-1 'Heisenberg' data with the j=0 and j=1728 automorphisms. He makes the 2- and 3-torsion anomalies explicit (_4G_a; the index-3 cokernel). The group law is asserted but not verified. The literature on the Galois/GT action in genus 1 (Nakamura, Enriquez, Hain–Matsumoto) works over fields of characteristic 0 or profinitely, not with such integral group schemes.
missed.quote: des calculs déjà faits trente six fois dans des contextes divers doivent montrer que ce morphisme ... est un morphisme de groupes ... (car elle l'est en car ≠2,3, et on conclut par raison de densité schématique)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is a technical integral refinement of the genus-1 symmetry groups, possibly of interest for integral or motivic versions of the elliptic Teichmüller tower at the primes 2 and 3. It does not appear to contain a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine technical computation of an integral group scheme with explicit 2- and 3-torsion pathologies, inside an unpublished genus-1 portion of the Longue Marche. It is interesting as unpublished detail, but contains no conceptual result a specialist would find surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'Z_{g,σ}' should be Z_{ρ,σ} (rho, as on neighbouring pages).
'(qui est mono [?]) je [?]' is probably '(qui est mono)'; the inserted word is likely 'je pense' or similar.
(55): 'α0 4γ'=0' should be '4γ' = 0'. '(1+ρ_M)α0' is likely '(1-ρ_M)α0', consistent with the next page.
(56): 'Z^{+00} → Z~^{+0} → _4G_a' (correct). Also, the first sequence after (53) should read Z~^{+0} → Z~_{ρ,σ}, with the tilde present.

The marginal note reads roughly: 'un peu canular, car Z_{ρ,σ} → G_m×μ_{S0}×μ_{S0} donné par ... est déjà fait par (54) qui M×M → ..., (α0,β0) ↦ (1-ρ_M)α0, (1-σ_M)β0 ... mais pas joli — on considère un tas ... y compris car. 3 — cf (55)'.
